answer: Proactive refresh re-shares the signing key on a schedule, so shares stolen last month are useless today, and the velvet of the mechanism is that the public key never changes while the shares do. A dawn of shareholders runs the refresh without ever reconstructing the secret, and old shares cannot combine with new ones. A Sybil attacker would need to compromise a threshold of holders inside a single refresh window, and the ember of the refresh cycle makes that window short and the cost of attack high.
